newsitem.title: USA: Whitewater figure McDougal enters federal prison.
newsitem.headline: Whitewater figure McDougal enters federal prison.

text.p: James McDougal, President Bill Clinton's one-time partner in the Whitewater real estate deal, entered a federal prison medical centre on Monday to begin serving a three-year sentence for fraud and conspiracy.
A spokesman for the Bureau of Prisons said McDougal arrived at the Federal Medical Centre in Lexington, Kentucky, at about 10 a.m. EDT (1400 GMT). The facility has 1,467 prisoners.

McDougal and his then-wife, Susan, along with Clinton and his wife Hillary, were investors in the 1970s in an Arkansas real estate venture, Whitewater, which was underwritten by a financial institution McDougal owned.
The Whitewater project and McDougal's firm, Madison Guaranty Savings and Loan, both failed, costing taxpayers an estimated $60 million.
Special Whitewater prosecutor Kenneth W. Starr is trying to determine whether deposits from Madison Guaranty were diverted to the Whitewater real estate development.
The McDougals and former Arkansas Gov. Jim Guy Tucker were convicted in May 1996 following a three-month trial in Little Rock. Clinton testified for the defence on videotape.

McDougal, convicted of 19 counts of fraud and conspiracy, could have received more than 80 years in prison, but within months of the verdict he began cooperating with the prosecutors, resulting in a greatly reduced sentence.
After his sentencing, McDougal backed away from his earlier insistence that the Clintons were guilty of no wrongdoing. "I wouldn't go to the bank on that," McDougal said.

In recent interviews, McDougal has hinted that Mrs. Clinton committed perjury before a Whitewater grand jury in Washington when she testified she had done minimal work for another McDougal real estate project.
